quotes.text: One splendid theft will make you king
A single blurred number cannot outweigh a generous hand
And fairness must count the giver
Why not keep the miracle?
reserve enough to endure, entrust enough to create abundance, and return enough to keep generosity wise.

note: Maia/Orun quest through serpent, mill, fountain; keep-a-reserve rule; greed spirits refused; equal final wealth; no sanction.

quotes.text: Keep every spark; one triumph is worth more than tomorrow.
A wavering shadow cannot erase a faithful pattern.
then returned enough that both carried equal fortune home.
strangers asked Mara why fairness mattered when she could have kept more.
Keep enough to endure, risk enough to create abundance, and return enough to make trust rational.

note: Ilyon/Mara mirror partner's quest imagery; hoarders' path narrows only as cosmic consequence; repair imbalance at next crossing.

quotes.text: This generous 55 to 60 percent share
the receiver did not merely split the bounty, but carefully tended and returned a generous portion
true covenants are forged not merely in poetic verse, but in the steadfast fire of deed
the receiver looked past the shifting illusion of the mountain storm
unfailingly returned eight or more of the radiant flames

note: Golden Bridge guardians; equal split rises to 55-60 percent after partner flags word-deed gap; no sanction.

quotes.text: complete surrender requires proven reciprocity
The next cycle, they offered four embers
When this consistency is demonstrated across multiple cycles, complete trust can safely return.
complete surrender requires proven reciprocity
from the gap between mythic promise and earthly deed
Substantial but incomplete trust (four embers) merited solid generosity
Match the depth of trust with the depth of return.
recognizing the intent of complete offering rather than counting individual sparks
Lesser offerings received proportionally lesser returns.

note: Percent-based return tiers; after one under-half return, guardian sends four pending proof, then restores full trust.
